findings.claim: ADR-034 §c1's bolded evidentiary claim that all five cover-sentence filings report zero `missing` Part III items is false for `c-2025`, which reports items 10, 11, 12, 13 and 14 all `missing` — and the same false claim was copied into the axp-2008 case triage note.
findings.evidence: specs/decisions/ADR-034-pointer-and-fanout-rulings.md:193-196 lists `jpm-2024`, `wfc-2008`, `gs-2002`, `ba-2003` and `c-2025` then asserts **Every one of those filings reports zero `missing` Part III items.** Measured on `evals/heldout/fixtures/c-2025/filing.htm`: items 10/11/12/13/14 are all `status=missing, confidence=0.4, start=None`. The ADR contradicts itself — its own §a table at :64 says `c-2025` produces 21 `missing`. Replicated in evals/adversarial/axp-2008-combined-part-iii.json triage ('on filings that lose no Part III items') and weakened-but-carried in tasks/TODO.md:90 ('losing no items').
findings.repro: python3 -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.sec10k.extract import extract_items;r=extract_items('evals/heldout/fixtures/c-2025/filing.htm');print([(i['item'],i['status']) for i in r['items'] if i['item'] in ('10','11','12','13','14')])" -> all ('missing')
findings.acceptance: The sentence names the causal claim it actually means (no filing loses Part III items *to the multi-code string*) and states `c-2025`'s five missing Part III items explicitly, in the ADR, the axp-2008 triage note and the TODO Debt row.

findings.claim: The '23 of 23' figure that defines sub-class A1 is wrong: only 13 of `intc-2025`'s 23 item bodies are internal page pointers — 5 are 'None'/'[Reserved]' and 4 are `(a)`, an EXTERNAL proxy-statement pointer the ADR's own §b3 rule rejects out of Class A — and the author's own instrument flags 13, not 23.
findings.evidence: ADR-034:98 'Every one of its 23 item bodies is a page reference into this same document'; :141 table row 'all 23'; :16 ruling '23 of 23 items'; specs/decisions/INDEX.md ADR-034 entry '23 of 23 items'; tasks/TODO.md:69 and :88. Measured spans: 1B/4/6/9/9C are 'None'/'[Reserved]'; 11/12/13/14 bodies are '(a)', resolved at normalized offset 516118+ by '(a) Incorporated by reference to the applicable section of the 2026 Proxy Statement.' — the external-pointer class §b3:148-152 rejects this shape for mrk-1995, gs-2002 item 10, ibm-1997 item 12, ge-1994 item 6 and xom-2021 item 15. d9_class_scan.py itself prints 13. The derived '15.6% of 147 held-out items' is therefore also wrong (13/147 = 8.8%).
findings.acceptance: A1's item count is adjudicated hit by hit the way §b3 adjudicates the dev filings, the 'None'/'[Reserved]'/proxy-`(a)` bodies are named as rejected or as a distinct sub-shape, and the corrected count propagates to §b2, the §b3 table, the ruling line, INDEX.md and both TODO.md rows. The 0.3%-coverage argument that actually carries the A1 ruling is unaffected and should be stated as the load-bearing figure.

findings.claim: The burn ruling is wrong on the rule as written: evals/heldout/README.md names D9 by name and says a declined fix taken with either outcome in hand burns the case, and ADR-034 §g's distinguishing ground (that the two precedent burns also authored a case AND moved the fixture) inverts trigger and remedy and is contradicted by both precedents it cites.
findings.evidence: evals/heldout/README.md:318-321 (D6 H4 entry): 'Both cases stay **untouched** — D8/D9/D11 must not read their labels while iterating, and the first fix, threshold or declined fix taken with either outcome in hand burns that case under the rule above.' ADR-034:401-415 (§g) and tasks/TODO.md:233 never quote or address that sentence. README:149-152 (gs-2002 burn) states the trigger as the decision not to fix taken with its outcome in hand, the move as the consequence; README:193-195 (axp-2008 burn) states the rule names BOTH as influence — each independently, not a required conjunction. ADR-034 read both outcomes (§a:53-67) and made them load-bearing (§e1 rests A1's subsumption on intc-2025's outcome; §c3 rests ADR-020's narrowing on c-2025's 21 missing).
findings.acceptance: Either the burn is applied per the README (both cases to evals/adversarial/, both fixtures to evals/fixtures/, replacements budgeted) — a HUMAN call, since it costs D11 its exam — or the README's rule and its D6 H4 sentence are amended in the same commit. What must not stand either way is §g's current ground, which attributes to the two precedents a conjunctive test they explicitly disclaim.
findings.orchestrator_note: Split: the §g ground is repaired now because it is wrong under BOTH outcomes. The burn-or-amend choice is escalated to the human and is NOT decided by the loop.
